topic: Kirchhoff's laws; node and mesh analysis
title: Two sources, two loops
instructions:
## Check your mesh analysis against the bench

Two supplies (V1 = 10 V on the left, V2 = 5 V on the right) feed a three-resistor network: R1 = 2 kΩ, R2 = 1 kΩ to ground from node `b`, R3 = 1 kΩ. Both sources have their positive terminal at the top.

## Do this

1. Solve the circuit on paper with node-voltage analysis at `b` (or two mesh equations).
2. Measure V(b), and the currents through R1, R2 and R3 with the ammeter. Note the sign: a negative reading means current flows against the arrow (from the second node to the first).
3. Answer the questions. Then confirm KCL at node b: the currents into b through R1 and R3 add up to the current out through R2.
hints: KCL at b: (10 − Vb)/2k + (5 − Vb)/1k = Vb/1k. Multiply by 2k: 10 − Vb + 10 − 2Vb = 2Vb, so 20 = 5Vb.
V2 supplies 1 mA and V1 supplies 3 mA; both deliver power here.

realityNote: On a real bench you would measure with one meter at a time, and the readings would differ by a percent or so because of resistor tolerance and the meter's own resistance. Paper, simulator and bench should agree within that.
